method: Convex hull of the 507 station positions of geometry:ta-sd-stations-strip-01 to -07 (17 vertices); a computed outline, not a published boundary. Frame: TASDPosition.dat (TA Collaboration data release on Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8405760, licence CC BY 4.0) lists 507 stations as x, y, z in km; the release states neither origin nor orientation. Both were established here by registering the table against a published map: Fig. 5 of arXiv:2103.01086 is a vector plot on latitude and longitude axes of the 507 TA SDs; its 507 red markers, read from the vector graphic and calibrated on the axis ticks, were matched one-to-one to the table and fitted to it. With the origin at the Central Laser Facility, 39.296918 N 112.908733 W (arXiv:1410.3151 section 5.1), x pointing east and y north, the fitted rotation is -0.001 deg and scale 1.0004, the CLF falls at table (0.006, 0.005) km, and the median residual is 14 m (90th percentile 26 m, 99th percentile 40 m) after a 6 m mean shift. A UTM zone 12 grid would be rotated by about 1.2 deg here, so the axes are true east and north. Stations are placed with an ellipsoidal azimuthal-equidistant projection about the CLF (WGS 84; agrees with a tangent-plane ENU to under 1 m at 25 km; a spherical equirectangular conversion would differ by up to 60 m at the array corners and fits the figure worse). The z column is not used. Each station is a 1.73 m square, the area-equivalent of one 3 m2 scintillator layer (arXiv:1201.4964: "Each layer of scintillator has an area of 3 m2"), so a position marker with the scintillator's area, not its outline. Accuracy 100 m covers the registration scatter, the origin (about 10 m) and the choice of projection.
name: Telescope Array surface-detector array outline (convex hull of the 507 stations)
notes: Area of the hull 691.5 km2 against the paper's "approximately 700 km2" (-1.2%).

summary.plain: The outline of the Telescope Array surface-detector array, about 690 square kilometres of Utah desert.
